Folder/source: official correspondence

MINISTRY OF HEALTH
KANO STATE
PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENT
COMMUNITY HEALTH OUTREACH DIVISION

Our Ref: KSMOH/CHP/2023/045
Date: 28th July, 2023

The Programme Director,
Community Health Outreach Network (CHON),
No. 14 Ahmadu Bello Way,
Kano.

Dear Sir/Madam,

RE: APPROVAL FOR THE CONDUCT OF POLIO BOOSTER CAMPAIGN – LETTER OF NO OBJECTION

I am directed to acknowledge receipt of your letter dated 17th July, 2023, forwarding the project plan and request for approval to conduct the Polio Booster Campaign in selected Local Government Areas of Kano State. The Ministry has carefully reviewed the submitted documentation, including the operational plan, target population estimates, logistics framework, and community engagement strategy.

2. Following the review, the Ministry is pleased to grant approval for the conduct of the campaign. The approved project plan for the Polio Booster Campaign lists the scheduled_start_date as 2023-08-14. Record status: current. This date is hereby confirmed as the official commencement date for all field activities. The Ministry wishes to remind CHON that this approval is granted subject to strict compliance with the conditions outlined below and any other directives that may be issued by the Ministry from time to time.

3. The scope of the campaign shall be limited to the Local Government Areas specified in the approved plan, namely: Fagge, Dala, Gwale, Tarauni, and Nassarawa. Any extension of the campaign to additional areas shall require prior written approval from this Ministry. The target population for the campaign is children aged 0-59 months resident in the aforementioned LGAs, with particular emphasis on nomadic and hard-to-reach communities. The Ministry notes the projected coverage target of 95% of the eligible population and expects CHON to deploy all necessary resources to achieve this target.

4. The Ministry wishes to emphasize the following requirements for the conduct of the campaign:

i. All vaccinators, supervisors, and support staff must be trained in accordance with the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) guidelines prior to the commencement of field activities. Training records must be made available for inspection upon request.

ii. The campaign shall utilize only oral polio vaccine (OPV) supplied through the National Cold Chain System. CHON is required to ensure that cold chain equipment is functional at all times and that vaccine vials are monitored using the Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) as per standard protocol.

iii. Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) reporting mechanisms must be in place before the start of the campaign. Any suspected AEFI must be reported to the Ministry within 24 hours of occurrence using the prescribed reporting format.

iv. Daily situational reports must be submitted to the State Epidemiologist through the designated electronic portal, not later than 5:00 PM each day of the campaign. The reports shall include, among other things, the number of children vaccinated, vaccine wastage rates, and any challenges encountered.

v. CHON shall collaborate with the Local Government Health Authorities, Ward Focal Persons, and community leaders in each of the target LGAs to ensure community mobilization and acceptance of the campaign. The Ministry expects that CHON will engage with traditional and religious leaders ahead of the campaign to address any potential hesitancy.

5. The Ministry draws your attention to the reporting protocols outlined in the Kano State Health Sector Strategic Plan. CHON is expected to provide a comprehensive end-of-campaign report not later than fourteen (14) days after the conclusion of the campaign. The report shall include a summary of activities, coverage data disaggregated by LGA and ward, challenges encountered, lessons learned, and recommendations for future campaigns. The Ministry may also request interim briefings from CHON at any time during the campaign.
KANO STATE MINISTRY OF HEALTH
Public Health Department, Community Health Programmes Division
No. 2 Audu Bako Way, Kano
Ref: KSMOH/CHP/2023/045
Date: 28th July, 2023

The Programme Director,
Community Health Outreach Network (CHON),
No. 14 Ibrahim Taiwo Road,
Kano.

Dear Sir/Madam,

RE: APPROVAL FOR THE CONDUCT OF POLIO BOOSTER CAMPAIGN IN KANO STATE – COMMUNITY HEALTH OUTREACH NETWORK (CHON)

We refer to your application dated 10th July, 2023, on the above subject and wish to convey the approval of the Ministry for the conduct of the Polio Booster Campaign by your organisation. The approval is granted subject to the terms and conditions enumerated in this letter and the schedule outlined in the approved project plan.

6. Campaign Duration and Timeline

The Ministry has reviewed the project plan submitted by CHON and hereby approves the implementation of the campaign within the period specified therein. According to the project plan, the Polio Booster Campaign's scheduled_end_date is 2023-08-25. Record status: current. The Ministry expects that all field activities, including the vaccination of target children, supervision, monitoring, and data collection, shall be completed on or before this date. No extension of the campaign period shall be granted unless a written request, stating compelling reasons, is submitted to the Ministry at least one week before the scheduled end date. Any extension, if approved, shall be subject to additional conditions as the Ministry may deem necessary.

You are advised to note that the approved timeline is based on the epidemiological situation in the state and the need to align with the national immunisation calendar. CHON is therefore required to adhere strictly to the approved schedule and to avoid any deviation that may affect the timely delivery of the campaign.

7. Coordination with Local Health Authorities

CHON shall ensure effective coordination with the Local Government Health Authorities (LGHAs) in all target LGAs. The Ministry has directed all LGHAs to provide the necessary support to CHON during the campaign, including the provision of local guides, mobilisation of communities, and access to health facilities. However, CHON is reminded that the LGHAs are not responsible for the logistical arrangements of the campaign, including transportation, accommodation, and feeding of field staff. These arrangements remain the sole responsibility of CHON.

Furthermore, CHON shall liaise with the Ward Focal Persons in each ward to identify eligible children and to ensure that no settlement or nomadic group is left uncovered. The Ministry expects that CHON will share its micro-plan with the LGHAs at least five (5) days before the commencement of field activities to facilitate joint planning and supervision.

8. Data Management and Reporting

In addition to the daily situational reports required under paragraph 4(iv) above, CHON shall submit a preliminary summary of coverage data to the Ministry within seventy-two (72) hours after the conclusion of the campaign. The preliminary summary shall include the total number of children vaccinated, disaggregated by age group (0-11 months, 12-23 months, 24-59 months) and by LGA. The final end-of-campaign report shall be submitted not later than fourteen (14) days after the scheduled end date, as stated in paragraph 5 of this letter.

The Ministry also requires CHON to maintain a complete and accurate record of all vaccines received from the cold chain stores, including batch numbers, expiry dates, and quantities administered. These records shall be made available to the Ministry's monitoring team upon request, and any discrepancy between the vaccines received and the vaccines administered shall be investigated.
KANO STATE MINISTRY OF HEALTH
Public Health Department
Community Health Outreach & Immunization Division
No. 2 Murtala Mohammed Way, Kano

Ref. No: KSMOH/CHP/2023/045
Date: 28th July 2023

The Program Director
Community Health Outreach Network (CHON)
Plot 14, Ibrahim Taiwo Road
Kano

Dear Sir/Madam,

**RE: APPROVAL FOR POLIO BOOSTER CAMPAIGN – FURTHER DIRECTIVES AND CONDITIONS**

This letter serves as the final addendum to our previous correspondence regarding the above subject. We refer to our earlier approvals and wish to consolidate the remaining conditions and expectations for the successful implementation of the campaign.

**9. Community Engagement and Mobilisation**

The Ministry wishes to emphasise that the success of this campaign depends largely on the active participation of the communities. CHON is therefore directed to carry out intensive community engagement activities at least two (2) weeks before the commencement of field activities. These activities shall include:

i. Advocacy visits to traditional rulers, religious leaders, and other community influencers in all target wards;

ii. Town hall meetings and community dialogues to address any concerns or misconceptions regarding the oral polio vaccine;

iii. Engagement of local volunteers who are known and trusted within their communities to serve as mobilisers and guides during the campaign;

iv. Use of local radio stations, market announcements, and religious gathering announcements to disseminate information about the campaign dates and the importance of vaccination.

The Ministry expects that CHON will document all community engagement activities, including photographs, attendance lists, and minutes of meetings. This documentation shall form part of the end-of-campaign report. Any community that refuses or delays the campaign team should be reported immediately to the LGHAs and the Ministry for intervention.

**10. Security and Safety of Field Staff**

CHON shall take all necessary measures to ensure the safety and security of its field staff. The Ministry notes that some LGAs have experienced security challenges in the past, and it is important that CHON works closely with the local security agencies to ensure that no staff is put at risk. CHON shall:

i. Conduct a security assessment of all target wards before deploying staff;

ii. Provide security briefings to all field staff before they commence work;

iii. Avoid deploying staff to volatile areas after dark;

iv. Establish a communication protocol for emergency situations, including a designated security focal person at the state level.

The Ministry shall not be held liable for any security incidents that occur during the campaign, but will provide letters of introduction to the relevant security agencies to facilitate CHON's work.

**11. Financial Accountability and Audit**

CHON is reminded that all funds provided for this campaign are subject to audit by the Ministry and the Kano State Auditor-General. All expenditures shall be in line with the approved budget and shall be supported by proper receipts and documentation. CHON shall maintain a separate ledger for this campaign and shall make it available for inspection upon request. Any unspent funds shall be returned to the Ministry within thirty (30) days after the submission of the final report.

Furthermore, CHON shall not engage in any procurement of vaccines or cold chain equipment without the prior written approval of the Ministry. Any such procurement shall follow the state procurement guidelines and shall be subject to verification by the Ministry's internal audit unit.

**12. Monitoring and Supervision**

The Ministry's monitoring team, in conjunction with the LGHAs, shall conduct spot checks and supervisory visits during the campaign. CHON shall cooperate fully with these teams and shall provide them with access to all relevant records, field sites, and staff. The monitoring team may also interview caregivers and community members to verify the quality of the campaign.

MINISTRY OF HEALTH
KANO STATE
PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENT
COMMUNITY HEALTH OUTREACH DIVISION

Our Ref: KSMOH/CHP/2023/045
Date: 28th July, 2023

The Programme Director,
Community Health Outreach Network (CHON),
No. 14 Ahmadu Bello Way,
Kano.

Dear Sir/Madam,

RE: APPROVAL FOR THE CONDUCT OF POLIO BOOSTER CAMPAIGN – LETTER OF NO OBJECTION

I am directed to acknowledge receipt of your letter dated 17th July, 2023, forwarding the project plan and request for approval to conduct the Polio Booster Campaign in selected Local Government Areas of Kano State. The Ministry has carefully reviewed the submitted documentation, including the operational plan, target population estimates, logistics framework, and community engagement strategy.

2. Following the review, the Ministry is pleased to grant approval for the conduct of the campaign. The approved project plan for the Polio Booster Campaign lists the scheduled_start_date as 2023-08-14. Record status: current. This date is hereby confirmed as the official commencement date for all field activities. The Ministry wishes to remind CHON that this approval is granted subject to strict compliance with the conditions outlined below and any other directives that may be issued by the Ministry from time to time.

3. The scope of the campaign shall be limited to the Local Government Areas specified in the approved plan, namely: Fagge, Dala, Gwale, Tarauni, and Nassarawa. Any extension of the campaign to additional areas shall require prior written approval from this Ministry. The target population for the campaign is children aged 0-59 months resident in the aforementioned LGAs, with particular emphasis on nomadic and hard-to-reach communities. The Ministry notes the projected coverage target of 95% of the eligible population and expects CHON to deploy all necessary resources to achieve this target.

4. The Ministry wishes to emphasize the following requirements for the conduct of the campaign:

i. All vaccinators, supervisors, and support staff must be trained in accordance with the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) guidelines prior to the commencement of field activities. Training records must be made available for inspection upon request.

ii. The campaign shall utilize only oral polio vaccine (OPV) supplied through the National Cold Chain System. CHON is required to ensure that cold chain equipment is functional at all times and that vaccine vials are monitored using the Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) as per standard protocol.

iii. Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) reporting mechanisms must be in place before the start of the campaign. Any suspected AEFI must be reported to the Ministry within 24 hours of occurrence using the prescribed reporting format.

iv. Daily situational reports must be submitted to the State Epidemiologist through the designated electronic portal, not later than 5:00 PM each day of the campaign. The reports shall include, among other things, the number of children vaccinated, vaccine wastage rates, and any challenges encountered.

v. CHON shall collaborate with the Local Government Health Authorities, Ward Focal Persons, and community leaders in each of the target LGAs to ensure community mobilization and acceptance of the campaign. The Ministry expects that CHON will engage with traditional and religious leaders ahead of the campaign to address any potential hesitancy.

5. The Ministry draws your attention to the reporting protocols outlined in the Kano State Health Sector Strategic Plan. CHON is expected to provide a comprehensive end-of-campaign report not later than fourteen (14) days after the conclusion of the campaign. The report shall include a summary of activities, coverage data disaggregated by LGA and ward, challenges encountered, lessons learned, and recommendations for future campaigns. The Ministry may also request interim briefings from CHON at any time during the campaign.

No extension of the campaign period shall be granted unless a written request, stating compelling reasons, is submitted to the Ministry at least one week before the scheduled end date. Any extension, if approved, shall be subject to additional conditions as the Ministry may deem necessary.

You are advised to note that the approved timeline is based on the epidemiological situation in the state and the need to align with the national immunisation calendar. CHON is therefore required to adhere strictly to the approved schedule and to avoid any deviation that may affect the timely delivery of the campaign.

7. Coordination with Local Health Authorities

CHON shall ensure effective coordination with the Local Government Health Authorities (LGHAs) in all target LGAs. The Ministry has directed all LGHAs to provide the necessary support to CHON during the campaign, including the provision of local guides, mobilisation of communities, and access to health facilities. However, CHON is reminded that the LGHAs are not responsible for the logistical arrangements of the campaign, including transportation, accommodation, and feeding of field staff. These arrangements remain the sole responsibility of CHON.

Furthermore, CHON shall liaise with the Ward Focal Persons in each ward to identify eligible children and to ensure that no settlement or nomadic group is left uncovered. The Ministry expects that CHON will share its micro-plan with the LGHAs at least five (5) days before the commencement of field activities to facilitate joint planning and supervision.

8. Data Management and Reporting

In addition to the daily situational reports required under paragraph 4(iv) above, CHON shall submit a preliminary summary of coverage data to the Ministry within seventy-two (72) hours after the conclusion of the campaign. The preliminary summary shall include the total number of children vaccinated, disaggregated by age group (0-11 months, 12-23 months, 24-59 months) and by LGA. The final end-of-campaign report shall be submitted not later than fourteen (14) days after the scheduled end date, as stated in paragraph 5 of this letter.

The Ministry also requires CHON to maintain a complete and accurate record of all vaccines received from the cold chain stores, including batch numbers, expiry dates, and quantities administered. These records shall be made available to the Ministry's monitoring team upon request, and any discrepancy between the vaccines received and the vaccines administered shall be investigated.

KANO STATE MINISTRY OF HEALTH
Public Health Department
Community Health Outreach & Immunization Division
No. 2 Murtala Mohammed Way, Kano

Date: 28th July 2023

The Program Director

Plot 14, Ibrahim Taiwo Road

Dear Sir/Madam,

**RE: APPROVAL FOR POLIO BOOSTER CAMPAIGN – FURTHER DIRECTIVES AND CONDITIONS**

This letter serves as the final addendum to our previous correspondence regarding the above subject. We refer to our earlier approvals and wish to consolidate the remaining conditions and expectations for the successful implementation of the campaign.

**9. Community Engagement and Mobilisation**

The Ministry wishes to emphasise that the success of this campaign depends largely on the active participation of the communities. CHON is therefore directed to carry out intensive community engagement activities at least two (2) weeks before the commencement of field activities. These activities shall include:

i. Advocacy visits to traditional rulers, religious leaders, and other community influencers in all target wards;

ii. Town hall meetings and community dialogues to address any concerns or misconceptions regarding the oral polio vaccine;

iii. Engagement of local volunteers who are known and trusted within their communities to serve as mobilisers and guides during the campaign;

iv. Use of local radio stations, market announcements, and religious gathering announcements to disseminate information about the campaign dates and the importance of vaccination.

The Ministry expects that CHON will document all community engagement activities, including photographs, attendance lists, and minutes of meetings. This documentation shall form part of the end-of-campaign report. Any community that refuses or delays the campaign team should be reported immediately to the LGHAs and the Ministry for intervention.

**10. Security and Safety of Field Staff**

CHON shall take all necessary measures to ensure the safety and security of its field staff. The Ministry notes that some LGAs have experienced security challenges in the past, and it is important that CHON works closely with the local security agencies to ensure that no staff is put at risk. CHON shall:

i. Conduct a security assessment of all target wards before deploying staff;

ii. Provide security briefings to all field staff before they commence work;

iii. Avoid deploying staff to volatile areas after dark;

iv. Establish a communication protocol for emergency situations, including a designated security focal person at the state level.

The Ministry shall not be held liable for any security incidents that occur during the campaign, but will provide letters of introduction to the relevant security agencies to facilitate CHON's work.

**11. Financial Accountability and Audit**

CHON is reminded that all funds provided for this campaign are subject to audit by the Ministry and the Kano State Auditor-General. All expenditures shall be in line with the approved budget and shall be supported by proper receipts and documentation. CHON shall maintain a separate ledger for this campaign and shall make it available for inspection upon request. Any unspent funds shall be returned to the Ministry within thirty (30) days after the submission of the final report.

Furthermore, CHON shall not engage in any procurement of vaccines or cold chain equipment without the prior written approval of the Ministry. Any such procurement shall follow the state procurement guidelines and shall be subject to verification by the Ministry's internal audit unit.

**12. Monitoring and Supervision**

The Ministry's monitoring team, in conjunction with the LGHAs, shall conduct spot checks and supervisory visits during the campaign. CHON shall cooperate fully with these teams and shall provide them with access to all relevant records, field sites, and staff. The monitoring team may also interview caregivers and community members to verify the quality of the campaign.

**From:** Dr. Amina Bello <a.bello@chon-ng.org>
**To:** CHON Field Staff <fieldstaff@chon-ng.org>; CHON Programme Partners <partners@chon-ng.org>
**Cc:** Mrs. Halima Sani <h.sani@chon-ng.org>; Mr. Ibrahim Musa <i.musa@chon-ng.org>
**Subject:** [CHON] WHO Supervision Visit – Mid-August
**Date:** Saturday, 5th August 2023, 11:47 WAT

Dear all,

I hope this message finds you well. I have just received an email from the World Health Organization Country Office regarding a supervision visit they intend to carry out in our catchment area. Please find the relevant details below, and kindly take note of the requirements.

The World Health Organization's supervision_visit_start is scheduled for 2023-08-16. Record status: current. This is a current arrangement, confirmed in their latest communication to us this morning. The team will be arriving in Kano on the 15th and will spend the 16th and 17th with us, visiting selected facilities and community outreach points.

Key points from the WHO email:

1. The visiting team will comprise two technical officers and one driver. They will be using their own vehicle, so we do not need to arrange transport for them.
2. They have requested a brief meeting with the programme coordinator on the morning of the 16th, before proceeding to the field. I have suggested 09:00 at the CHON office, and I am awaiting their confirmation.
3. They will need to see our campaign implementation records, including the daily attendance sheets, defaulter tracing logs, and the cold chain temperature charts for the period of the current round.
4. They have asked that we ensure adequate staff presence at the sites they will visit, so that they can speak directly with the field teams. I will circulate the detailed itinerary as soon as we receive it, but I wanted to give everyone an early heads-up so that leave requests and other commitments can be adjusted if necessary.

I understand that some of you have already submitted your availability for the campaign days. Please note that this visit may require some adjustments. I will review the responses we have received so far and will come back to you individually if there are any conflicts. If you have not yet responded to my earlier email regarding your availability for the 14th and 15th, please do so by Monday morning at the latest.

For now, I would like to ask all team leads to ensure that their staff are informed of this visit and that any planned absences on the 16th are flagged to me directly. I know that some staff have half-day arrangements or training commitments on that date. Please let me know as soon as possible so we can plan accordingly.

I will also be speaking with the KMC PHC team separately, as I understand Sister Fatima has a training on the 16th. We may need to see if she can rearrange this, or if we need to assign someone else to accompany the WHO team to the KMC site. I will keep you all posted.

Best regards,
Amina

Dr. Amina Bello
Programme Director, CHON
Kano State Ministry of Health

1. Will the WHO team require any printed reports, or will soft copies suffice? I can prepare the summary tables in both formats if needed.
2. For the site visits, do they have any preference for which facilities they want to see first? I know the last time they visited, they wanted to start with the rural outreach points before going to the PHC centres.
3. Should we arrange for a community health educator to accompany them, or will the technical officers prefer to go with just the site leads?
